question: Warren Hastings’ experiment of auctioning the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder is almost similar to
solution:
Warren Hastings’ experiment of auctioning the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder is almost similar to __**Ijara system of the Mughals.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Warren Hastings**, the Governor-General of British India from 1773 to 1785, implemented an experiment known as the auctioning of the right to collect revenue.
 
• Under this system, the British East India Company would auction off the revenue-collecting rights of a specific region to the** highest bidder.**
 
• The **Ijara system,** on the other hand, was a revenue collection system used by the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• In the Ijara system, the **Mughal rulers** would lease out revenue collection rights to individuals or groups, who were responsible for collecting and remitting a fixed amount of revenue from a particular region.
 
• While there are similarities between Hastings' auctioning system and the Ijara system, they differ in certain key aspects.
 
• Both systems involved leasing revenue collection rights, but the mechanisms and objectives were distinct.
 
• **Hastings' auction system** aimed to maximize revenue for the British East India Company.
 
• The highest bidder won the rights to collect revenue and was expected to pay the bid amount upfront, making it a competitive process focused on generating immediate income for the Company.
 
• In contrast, the Ijara system of the Mughals focused on stability and regular revenue collection.
 
• The** leaseholders** in the Ijara system were responsible for maintaining law and order in their assigned regions and ensuring the smooth collection of revenue.
 
• Their role was not solely profit-oriented but involved broader governance responsibilities.
 
• 
 
Therefore, while there may be similarities between Hastings' auctioning system and the Ijara system of the Mughals in terms of revenue collection through leasing rights, their underlying objectives and mechanisms differed significantly.

 

Thus we conclude that Warren Hastings’ experiment of auctioning the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder is almost similar to **Ijara system of the Mughals.**__
